findings.title: Runbook MCP executor allows arbitrary shell command execution
findings.description: The runbook executor takes arbitrary shell commands from parsed Markdown blocks and executes them. Without command allowlisting or sandboxing, any user who can call the MCP tool can execute arbitrary commands on the host.
findings.evidence: The executor receives `block.Content` directly and passes it to shell execution. No allowlist, no sandbox, no argument validation.
findings.impact: Remote code execution on the runbook-mcp service host.
findings.remediation: Implement a capabilities-based allowlist: only permit specific commands (kubectl, helm, curl). Use argument validation with regex. Consider running in a sidecar container with dropped capabilities. Add `safe_mode` flag.

findings.title: PR Bridge GitHub API client has no endpoint allowlist
findings.description: The GitHub client uses a configurable base URL with no validation. Subdomain or path injection could redirect API calls to an attacker-controlled endpoint.
findings.evidence: Base URL is set from config. No validation that the URL matches a known GitHub domain.
findings.impact: Credential exfiltration via malicious API endpoint.
findings.remediation: Pin GitHub API base URL to `api.github.com`. Reject custom URLs. Validate via string comparison, not regex.

findings.title: Error messages may leak internal paths into logs
findings.description: Several error types include `fmt.Errorf` with operation and workload names. If these propagate to HTTP responses, internal details are exposed.
findings.evidence: `finops/errors.go` wraps errors with op+workload. `anomstack/consumer.go` wraps parse errors with full context.
findings.impact: Information disclosure: internal paths, struct fields, workload names.
findings.remediation: Use `%v` for user-facing errors. Log full details with `slog` at Debug level. Return generic HTTP errors to callers.

findings.title: No rate limiting on FinOps recommendation endpoint
findings.description: POST /api/v1/waste/:id/recommend creates PRs via GitHub API. No rate limiting means an attacker could burn through GitHub API quota or create spam PRs.
findings.evidence: POST handler calls `GenerateRecommendation` which calls `prSvc.GenerateRightSizePR`. No rate limiter middleware.
findings.impact: GitHub API abuse, spam PR generation.
findings.remediation: Add a token-bucket rate limiter (1 request per 10 seconds per user/IP). Use golang.org/x/time/rate.

findings.title: PR Bridge error responses include branch and repo details
findings.description: When PR creation fails, the error returned may include branch names, repo paths, and PR details that reveal internal project structure.
findings.evidence: Errors include `repo`, `new_branch`, `title` fields from the PR request.
findings.impact: Information disclosure of internal repository structure.
findings.remediation: Map domain errors to sanitized HTTP responses. Log internal details server-side only.

findings.title: Anomstack event summary may contain unescaped content
findings.description: The AnomstackEvent.Summary field is stored and forwarded as-is. If consumed by a web UI without sanitization, XSS is possible.
findings.evidence: Summary is passed directly from upstream alert payload. No sanitization at receive time.
findings.impact: Cross-site scripting if events are displayed in a dashboard.
findings.remediation: Sanitize the Summary field at receive time: strip HTML tags, truncate to 1024 chars, validate with a strict allowlist.

findings.title: No authorization check on FinOps API endpoints
findings.description: The recommendation and dismissal endpoints lack any auth middleware. Any caller can trigger PR creation or dismiss observations.
findings.evidence: No auth middleware, no API key validation, no user context in request scope.
findings.remediation: Add Bearer token or OAuth2 middleware. Use claims to verify caller has `finops:write` scope for mutating endpoints.

findings.title: No CSRF protection on HTTP endpoints
findings.description: None of the services implement CSRF tokens. This is low risk for internal services but relevant if exposed via ingress.
findings.evidence: No CSRF middleware or SameSite cookie configuration found.
findings.impact: Potential CSRF if services are exposed via browser-facing ingress.
findings.remediation: Add SameSite=Strict cookies for session endpoints. Use Origin/Referer validation on mutating POST endpoints.

findings.title: No request size limits on webhook endpoints
findings.description: Webhook and POST endpoints have no body size limit. An attacker could send a large payload to exhaust memory.
findings.impact: Denial of service via memory exhaustion.

findings.title: Structured slog logging may still need context propagation
findings.description: Services use `slog` properly, but some log calls don't include request-scoped trace IDs. Multi-tenant environments need correlation IDs in every log line.
findings.evidence: Most log calls include context from OTEL spans, but middleware-level request ID injection is not present.
findings.impact: Difficult to correlate logs across services during incident response.
findings.remediation: Add HTTP middleware that injects X-Request-ID into slog context. Ensure slog.Handler adds this field to every log line.

positive_findings: All Go code uses parameterized SQL queries via pgx/sqlx — no raw SQL concatenation (SEC-004 related: injection-resistant at DB layer)
Secrets are read from environment variables (GH_TOKEN via ExternalSecrets pattern) — no hardcoded tokens
OTEL spans are present in all critical code paths — observability baseline met
Error sentinels use typed struct errors with proper %w wrapping — no raw string errors
No `interface{}` or `any` types in exported function signatures — type safety maintained
k8s manifests use securityContext with runAsNonRoot, readOnlyRootFilesystem, drop all caps — pod security baseline met
recommendations: IMMEDIATE: Add command allowlist to runbook-mcp executor (SEC-001)
HIGH: Pin GitHub API base URL and add endpoint validation to pr-bridge (SEC-002)
HIGH: Sanitize error messages before HTTP response serialization (SEC-003, SEC-005)
MEDIUM: Add rate limiter middleware to finops-analyzer POST endpoints (SEC-004)
MEDIUM: Add auth middleware with RBAC to all mutating endpoints (SEC-007)
MEDIUM: Sanitize AnomstackEvent.Summary at receive time (SEC-006)
LOW: Add http.MaxBytesReader to all endpoints (SEC-009)
LOW: Add request ID middleware across all services (SEC-010)
